title: v2 session idle timeout is too aggressive for a build-and-test cycle, silently hands device to another claimant
description:
Observed during demix T-LU-576 (bundle-id rename verification, 2026-09-06): a
simemu v2 `claim ios` session (form_factor=phone) expired after roughly
30-60 seconds of idle time between `simemu do <session> ...` calls -- well
under the reported `expires_at` TTL (~20 minutes). Sequence observed:

1. `simemu claim ios` -> session s-XXXXX, expires_at ~20 min out.
2. A few `simemu do` calls (env, install, launch) succeed.
3. ~1-2 minutes spent reading/writing source code between calls (no `do`
   calls issued).
4. Next `simemu do <session> ...` call returns
   `{"error": "session_expired", "hint": "Session expired after
   inactivity. Re-claim with: simemu claim ios"}` even though `expires_at`
   was still ~18 minutes away.
5. Re-claiming sometimes returned the SAME device (arugula, iPhone Air,
   iOS 26.4) with no visible ownership conflict. But later in the same
   task, after another idle gap, a raw `xcrun simctl` screenshot (issued
   directly against the device UDID, not through a simemu `do` call,
   because the just-expired claim made scripting the next simemu call
   awkward) showed a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT APP in the foreground
   (com.fitkind's onboarding screen) -- meaning another agent's concurrent
   task had claimed and was actively driving the SAME shared device while
   this session believed (and had recent evidence) that it still owned it.

Impact: a lapsed claim silently hands the device to another concurrent
task. Any evidence (screenshots, notification delivery, UI state)
captured after a claim has silently expired is UNTRUSTWORTHY -- it may
belong to a different agent's unrelated test run. This is a false-evidence
risk, not just an inconvenience: an agent that doesn't notice the
`session_expired` error (e.g. if it's buried in output, or if it falls
back to raw `xcrun simctl` calls against a remembered UDID instead of
going through `simemu do`) can silently attribute a completely different
app's state to its own task.

Ask: either (a) raise the effective idle timeout for v2 `claim`/`do`
sessions to something that tolerates a normal think-then-act cadence
(minutes, not tens of seconds) -- these are AI agents that read/write
source, build, and reason between simulator interactions, not humans
tapping continuously -- or (b) make the idle timeout configurable at
claim time, or (c) at minimum make `session_expired` impossible to miss
(e.g. `simemu do` should refuse to silently succeed with a stale
UDID-based fallback, and any doc/skill guidance should say explicitly:
never fall back to raw `xcrun simctl` on a remembered UDID after a claim
expires -- re-claim first).

Reported by: build-bundleid (demix session), relayed via team-lead.

See also: T-LU-054 (reaping keyed to claimant PID rather than device-in-use -- same subsystem, root-cause angle) and T-056 (no on-demand release verb exists for v2 sessions at all -- same subsystem, opposite failure direction: this task is about reaping TOO EAGERLY, T-056 is about having NO voluntary way to release).
acceptanceCriteria: A v2 claim session survives at least 5 minutes of no "do" calls without expiring, given its expires_at TTL has not elapsed
session_expired is either impossible to miss (loud, not buried) or the CLI refuses a raw-UDID fallback path so agents cannot silently act on a device they no longer hold
proofRequirements: Repro script: claim, wait 90s with no do calls, issue a do call, confirm it succeeds (or, if the design is unchanged, confirm the error is now impossible to miss)
